Based on the latest information, India's current repo rate is 5.50%, and it was last changed on October 7, 2026 — which is today. 
 [1]

The Recent Rate Hike

The RBI raised its key repo rate by 25 basis points (0.25%) at its October 2026 monetary policy meeting, marking the first rate hike since February 2023. 
 [1]
 This brought the rate from 5.25% to 5.50%.

Why the Rate Was Increased

The RBI made this decision amid rising inflationary pressures. Annual inflation had accelerated to 4.82% in August 2026, which was the highest level since December 2024 and rose above the RBI's 4% inflation target for the third consecutive month. 
 [1]
 Contributing factors included:

A weakening rupee
Higher crude oil prices (above $100 per barrel)
Global uncertainty from geopolitical tensions in the Middle East
Rate hikes by other major central banks, including the U.S. Federal Reserve

The RBI also raised the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate to 5.75% and the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate to 5.25% in conjunction with this hike.
